title: Classifying and sharing data safely
summary: Our data classes, what you may do with each, and safe ways to share files with colleagues, customers and vendors.
body_md:
## Four classes of information

| Class | Examples | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Public** | Website content, published blog posts | Share freely |
| **Internal** | Org charts, internal wiki, project plans | Staff only; not outside without approval |
| **Confidential** | Customer data, contracts, financials, source code | Need to know; approved tools only; encrypted |
| **Restricted** | Passwords and keys, Aadhaar/PAN, health or payment data, security reports | Smallest group possible; never in email or chat |

When unsure, treat information as **Confidential**.

## Sharing safely

- **Use approved tools** (the company drive or document system) with access limited to named people. Avoid
  "anyone with the link" for anything above Public.
- **Check the recipient** before you hit send; autocomplete is the most common cause of data leaks.
- **Don't move work data to personal accounts**, personal email, personal cloud storage or USB drives.
- **Share the minimum.** Send a filtered report rather than a full customer export.
- **Vendors get data only under a contract** that the security or legal team has approved.

## Personal data

Under DPDP, we may use personal data only for the purpose it was collected for, keep it only as long as needed, and
protect it with reasonable safeguards. Don't copy customer data into spreadsheets for convenience, and delete
extracts once you're done.

## Printing and screens

Collect printouts straight away, shred confidential paper, lock your screen when you step away and watch out for
shoulder-surfing in public places.

What's the safest way to share a contract with a customer?
options: A company drive link limited to the customer's named contacts
A public 'anyone with the link' share

quiz.q: A colleague asks you to send them the database password over chat. What do you do?
options: Refuse; restricted secrets go only through the approved secrets manager
Send half in chat and half by email
Post it in the team channel

quiz.q: You need customer data for an analysis. What's best?
options: Request only the fields you need, and delete the extract afterwards
Copy it to personal cloud storage
